notes: Covers the municipal budget only. School-district and county taxes on the same property-tax bill belong to separate governments and are not included.
Insurance, pension and social-security contributions and shared-service payments ($57,923,625) are spread across departments in proportion to their size.
The reserve for uncollected taxes ($1,091,031) is set aside, not spent, so it is not counted as spending.

Political money counts PAC, business and union contributions to candidates for Bayonne City municipal office and mayor reported to NJ ELEC since 2022-10-01. Individual donors ($244,550 in the same period), candidates' own committees and party committees are not counted. Small campaigns may file without itemizing, so some contributions may not appear.
Contractor pay-to-play disclosures and transparency practices have not been loaded yet; transparency is not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-01. Data center deals and corporate lobbying come from a hand-checked list of news reports and public records. A town with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

Red flags: 5 license-plate cameras are mapped inside Bayonne City's borders in OpenStreetMap (4 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the town is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 4 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside Bayonne City's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

source.label: OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock)

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Bayonne Police Department has an automated license plate reader program, according to an audit released in July 2025 by the New Jersey State Police.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS016361, citing New Jersey State Police
